newsitem.title: HUNGARY: US INTER-CONTINENTAL TO BUY HUNGARY'S HOTEL FORUM.
newsitem.headline: US INTER-CONTINENTAL TO BUY HUNGARY'S HOTEL FORUM.

text.p: The U.S's Inter-Continental Corporation will buy Forum Szalloda Rt, a four-star hotel in downtown Budapest, Hungary's state privatisation agency APV Rt said in statement on Wednesday.
The buyer will pay $49.4 million or 190 percent of the face value for the 94.91 percent stake, the statement said.
The remaining stake will be offered to employees at a 50 percent discount to the 190 percent purchase price, the statement said, adding that employees can pay partly by compensation coupons .
The buyer plans to invest $11 million and plans to upgrade it to a five-star status within three years and will operate the hotel under the Inter-Continental name, the statement said.
The U.S. buyer undertook to continue to employ the current staff for one year.

In 1995 Prime Minister Gyula Horn cancelled an already completed deal under which the U.S.' American General Hospitality was to pay $57.1 million for a 51 percent stake in HungarHotels, which then included 14 other hotels in addition to Forum.
Hungary first attempted to sell HungarHotels' flagship Forum Szalloda separately in February 1996, when 15 companies submitted bids, but the tender was declared unsuccessful.
The hotel was sold in the present private tender with three invited bidders of which two placed bids.
Last week an 85 percent stake in the other hotels, grouped into Hungaria Szalloda Rt, was sold to Danubius .
Since 1992 Hungary has been awarding compensation coupons to victims of expropriations and persecution by Hungary's former fascist and communist governments.
The coupons have a lively secondary market. On the Budapest Stock Exchange they closed at 431 forints, up 12, on Wednesday.
The sale of Forum marks Inter-Continental's return to the Hungarian market after four years.

Inter-Continental operated one of Budapest's most distinguieshed downtown hotels for than 20 years in franchise, until the U.S Marriott Corp bought the hotel for $53 million following a tender in 1992, where Inter-Continental was among the bidders.
